data.title: Microsoft Won't Renew Deal for Renting AI Cloud Capacity From Oracle: Report — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Shares of Oracle were under pressure Friday following a report that said Microsoft was bringing to an end an agreement to rent artificial-intelligence computing capacity from Oracle.

Oracle stock dropped 1.3% to $113.55 after the report from Bloomberg, which cited "people familiar with the matter."

Microsoft stock fell 0.6% to $532.55 as the AI trade was staging a bit of a comeback Friday following a brutal selloff in the previous session.

An Oracle spokesperson neither confirmed nor denied the Bloomberg report to Barron's and said in a statement that demand for Oracle's AI cloud infrastructure "remains strong."

The spokesperson added there was ongoing demand for its earlier-generation graphic processing units, or GPUs, which "demonstrates the continued demand and durable value of our infrastructure."

Microsoft didn't respond to requests for comment from Barron's.

In recent months, Microsoft has stopped using rented computing capacity from Oracle and has decided against renewing their contract, according to Bloomberg. The deal between Microsoft and Oracle dates back to late 2023, when Oracle announced a multi-year agreement with Microsoft for the software company to use its cloud infrastructure.

The report from Bloomberg with Wall Street focused on the massive capital spending on AI from the Big Tech hyperscalers.

Concerns also have risen on Wall Street around the possibility that the Democratic Party's big win in the midterm elections could mean heightened AI buildout regulation.

With Democrats taking control of Congress, stocks with exposure to AI data centers have absolutely been hammered. But Wall Street seems assured that the AI trade weakness is just a near-term blip.

"We expect near-term volatility in AI infrastructure companies over the next several weeks," William Blair analysts Tim Mulrooney and Jed Dorsheimer said in a research note following the midterms.

Morgan Stanley analyst Ariana Salvatore added in a research note there's likely to be near-term volatility that will weigh most heavily on AI stocks given the potential for more durable and broader restrictions at the local and federal level.

Salvatore, however, doesn't believe the negative sentiment in the stock market will last long.

Write to Kit Norton at kit.norton@barrons.com

data.title: Canada's Carney Eyes Expanding Breadth of Trade With China
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canadian and Chinese officials are a mulling a further deepening of trade ties after striking a deal focused on agriculture and electric vehicles earlier this year, Prime Minister Mark Carney said.

"We are in discussions with the Chinese about where to next on trade," Carney said at a press conference in Winnipeg, Manitoba, to promote measures unveiled in the government's annual budget plan. He added Beijing agreed this week to extend trade relief for Canadian agricultural products, most notably canola, until the end of 2028.

The Carney-led Liberal government has worked to reset relations with China following years of tumult under former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. Early in 2026, Carney met Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing, and in exchange for removing tariffs on Canadian agrifood goods, Ottawa agreed to allow the importation of up to 49,000 electric vehicles - a move that angered some Trump administration officials.

Carney added he's scheduled to meet with Xi at the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders summit in Shenzen. "We have more opportunities to provide greater stability to that relationship ... but also to expand the breadth of the trading relationship." Prior to that, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng is arriving in Canada next week for a meeting with Canadian officials.

Resetting trade ties with China is part of the Carney government's policy goal to diversify its exports and reduce the country's reliance on the U.S. to drive growth. Up until President Trump's second term, roughly three-quarters of all Canadian exports were U.S.-bound. Trade data covering the first three quarters of 2026 indicate that the U.S. accounted for 68% of all Canadian sales abroad.

data.title: CES Energy Solutions Corp. Announces Amendment, Extension and Upsize of Its Credit Facility
data.description:
CES Energy Solutions Corp. (“CES” or the “Company”) () () is pleased to announce that it has successfully entered into an amended and restated credit agreement dated November 6, 2026 (the “Amended and Restated Credit Agreement”), with respect to its syndicated and operating credit facilities (the “Credit Facility”). The syndicate is led by The Bank of Nova Scotia as Agent, Lead Arranger and Joint Bookrunner, together with The Toronto-Dominion Bank, Bank of Montreal, ATB Financial, and National Bank of Canada as Joint Bookrunners, and also includes Wells Fargo Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, and Business Development Bank of Canada. The total size of the Credit Facility has increased to approximately C$750.0 million equivalent. The Credit Facility, which matures on November 6, 2031, is secured by substantially all of the Company’s assets and includes customary terms, conditions and covenants.

“The upsized Credit Facility and improved terms are consistent with the increased size, scale and credit profile of CES, and reflect the strength of our financial attributes and recent rating agency upgrades. The expansion to $750.0 million from $550.0 million provides ample liquidity to support the increased size and scope of our business as we continue to move through our growth inflection phase. The new five-year term locks in current attractive terms and is aligned with our identified business needs, potential expansion opportunities, and return of capital initiatives. We thank the syndicate members for their strong participation in our upsized Credit Facility and for their ongoing partnership,” said Anthony Aulicino, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Highlights of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement

  • Total facility size increased by $200.0 million, for an aggregate Credit Facility of approximately C$ equivalent $750.0 million;

  • Single syndicated revolving credit facility of C$ equivalent $702.0 million, with a co-borrower structure allowing for draws in either Canada or the U.S., in either currency;

  • Canadian-based C$20.0 million operating facility and U.S.-based US$20.0 million operating facility;

  • Accordion feature of C$ equivalent $350.0 million; and

  • Removal of the Total Net Debt to EBITDA covenant and improved non-financial covenant baskets, aligned with the higher credit quality and increased size and scope of the Company.

A redacted copy of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement will be available on CES’ SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca in accordance with National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations, as adopted by the Canadian securities regulatory authorities.

About CES Energy Solutions Corp.
CES Energy Solutions is a leading provider of technically advanced consumable chemical solutions to the energy industry. These products and services are deployed at the drill-bit, at the point of completion and stimulation, at the wellhead and pump-jack to support ongoing production needs, and finally through to the pipeline and midstream market. These chemical solutions are instrumental in allowing the oil and gas industry to maximize returns in an environment of steadily increasing service intensity and advanced technical requirements. CES’ business model is asset light and requires limited re-investment capital to operate and grow. As a result, CES has been able to capitalize on the growing market demand for drilling fluids and production and specialty chemicals in North America while generating strong free cash flow.

Additional information about CES is available at www.sedarplus.ca or on the Company’s website at www.cesenergysolutions.com.

data.title: Gold drops as strong US payrolls boost dollar, yields
data.description:
Key points:
  • US job growth beats expectations in October
  • Bullion on track for best week since late August
  • Price dip spurs gold buying in India ahead of Diwali
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly gains

By Anushree Mukherjee

Gold prices fell on Friday after stronger-than-expected US payrolls data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer, boosting the dollar and Treasury yields.

Spot gold fell 0.3% to $4,074.36 per ounce by 01:54 p.m. ET (1854 GMT). The metal fell by more than 1% to hit a low of $4,033.29 earlier in the session.

Spot gold was up 5.2% for the week, on track for its best week since August.

US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.9% lower at $4,074.90.

The US dollar rose 0.7% to its highest level since October 29, making dollar-denominated gold more expensive for holders of other currencies, while benchmark 10-year Treasury yields also climbed.

"Gold gapped lower on a stellar employment report (that was) strong across the board, but is trying to claw back higher. This is a litmus test for this week's rally," independent metals trader Tai Wong said.

US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting the labor market remained resilient and giving the Federal Reserve more scope to focus on inflation stemming from the Middle East conflict.

Traders currently see an 81% chance that the Fed will raise rates in December, compared with 72.8% before the payrolls report, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher interest rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, making gold less attractive to investors.

Brent crude was on track for a sharp weekly drop on expectations of a de-escalation in the US-Iran war after midterm election results, although persistent Middle East supply concerns continued to support prices.

Two Federal Reserve officials on Thursday backed small, steady rate hikes to rein in above-target inflation.

On the physical front, lower gold prices encouraged Indian retail buying ahead of the key Diwali festival. Gold had dropped to a one-year low of $3,869.85 an ounce on October 30.

Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.8% to $52.18, platinum gained 1.6% to $1,541.42, while palladium fell 0.6% to $1,024.59. All three were poised for weekly gains.

data.title: What If the Only Companies That Let Their Stocks Be Tokenized Are Crypto Firms? — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Joe Light

The tokenized stock market planned by crypto firm OKX and New York Stock Exchange-owner Intercontinental Exchange has run into a major roadblock. The problem? Companies outside the crypto industry are saying no.

As of the latest public notice, every non-crypto-tied stock issuer originally announced by the venue had objected to being included. The only firms listed on the original notice that have not objected are Coinbase Global, Robinhood Markets, Circle Internet Group, Strategy, Securitize and BitGo, all of which have ties to the crypto industry.

Securitize said it plans to allow its shares to be traded on the platform. Spokespeople for OKX, Robinhood and Circle declined to comment. ICE and the rest of the companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

"We're encouraged by the companies that have chosen to participate and hope more issuers will follow their lead as they better understand the opportunity," said Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo in a statement.

Crypto and Wall Street firms in the past couple months have moved forward rapidly with projects that turn traditional assets like stocks and bonds into "tokens" powered by the same technology underlying cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin.

The goal isn't to make stocks as volatile as crypto but to replace some of the intermediaries and traditional processes that make trades slow to settle with "blockchain" technology that allows for near-instant transfers and settlements. Proponents of the shift say that tokenized markets could enable 24/7 stock trading and reduce collateral needs, among other benefits.

The issuer objections are part of a process the Securities and Exchange Commission established for firms that want to create "tokenized securities venues" that don't have to comply with all the rules that typically apply to exchanges. As part of the process, the SEC required that the venues give stock issuers a chance to object to being listed.

OKXICE in its original notice included 62 companies whose shares it planned to list. All but six of them have now objected, according to its updated public notices. The company has received 11 additional objections from companies that weren't on the earlier list. OKXICE hasn't updated its public notices to show the complete list of firms it's reached out to. So it's unclear whether there are additional stocks that could appear on the venue that aren't in the public notices.

The spate of objections doesn't mean that tokenization is dead on Wall Street, but it is a sign that issuers will need more convincing about OKXICE's model.

Shortly after the venue was announced, OKXICE co-chairman and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo told Barron's he anticipated there being objections from issuers who didn't yet understand the benefits of the project and were concerned with how their stocks might trade on the new exchange.

Last month a spokesperson for one of the objectors, Applied Optoelectronics, said that the company was concerned that the OKXICE venue could impact its stock's pricing, liquidity, and volatility.

Other stock tokenization projects don't need issuer consent and have already launched. A service run by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp. launched in late October allowing institutions to turn about $30 trillion worth of securities into tokens. Unlike the proposed OKXICE venue, that project doesn't affect retail investors directly and instead involves how institutions can move shares around after a trade has happened.

Retail investors may yet see their own shares get tokenized, but the companies who issue the stocks will have to hold off on objecting first.

Write to Joe Light at joe.light@barrons.com

data.title: Honda Unveils Fully Redesigned CBR1000RR-R Fireblade Supersport Model in World Premiere
data.description:
Milan, Italy, Nov 7, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Honda today presented the fully redesigned CBR1000RR-R Fireblade series, its flagship supersport motorcycle, as a 2027 model at EICMA 2026 (Milan Motorcycle Show. press days: November 3-4; public days: November 5-8), held in Milan, Italy.

The CBR1000RR-R Fireblade series, Honda's flagship supersport motorcycle range, has been developed under the concept of "Total Control for the Track," with the aim of delivering its full potential on the racetrack. For the fully redesigned 2027 model, Honda has further pursued racing victories and the joy of riding, newly designing approximately 75% of the motorcycle's components to further enhance its competitiveness on the track.

The 2027 lineup consists of three variants: the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade (Fireblade), the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP (Fireblade SP), equipped with electronically controlled suspension and other features, and the newly introduced CBR1000RR-R Fireblade HRC Works Edition (HRC Works Edition).

The HRC Works Edition has been newly introduced as a homologation model for the FIM*1 Superbike World Championship (WSBK). It features dedicated components, including front winglets designed to enhance aerodynamic performance and cornering capability. The model is also designed to be road-legal through compliance with the regulations of individual markets.

Key features of the CBR1000RR-R Fireblade series

Chassis and suspension

For the 2027 model, Honda sought to combine outstanding cornering performance and chassis stability during acceleration and deceleration on the racetrack with agile handling and greater freedom of control on public roads.

The newly designed aluminum twin-tube frame achieves an ideal balance of rigidity. The opening in the head pipe, which channels fresh air to the air cleaner, has been enlarged to optimize lateral rigidity. In addition, the engine cylinder hangers have been changed from the previous one-piece cast structure with integrated stiffeners to a bolt-on configuration using separate brackets. This provides greater flexibility in frame design and, together with refinements to various components, reduces lateral rigidity by 20% compared with the previous model while maintaining torsional rigidity.

These changes improve cornering performance, tire contact feel, and stability under acceleration, achieving an advanced balance of handling performance on both the racetrack and public roads.

Furthermore, the use of a thin-wall gravity die casting (GDC) process enables highly precise rigidity tuning, allowing the frame to be formed with a minimum wall thickness of just 2mm. By optimizing wall thickness throughout the frame, Honda has achieved a weight reduction of 440g compared with the previous model.*2

The aluminum pressed-construction swingarm has also been redesigned. The pivot shaft diameter has been reduced from 20mm to 17mm, while wall thickness and pivot width have been adjusted to optimize rigidity. By reducing lateral rigidity by 12% while maintaining torsional rigidity, the new swingarm improves rear tire contact feel during cornering.

Suspension damping settings have been optimized for each variant to improve performance on the racetrack while enhancing the suspension's ability to follow road surface irregularities during everyday riding.

- Fireblade: Retains the SHOWA (Astemo, Ltd.) Big Piston Fork (BPF) at the front and SHOWA BFRC-lite suspension at the rear.

- Fireblade SP: Continues to feature electronically controlled Ohlins suspension, with NXP Smart-EC3.0 at the front and TTX36 Smart-EC3.0 at the rear.

To further reduce vehicle weight, a titanium fuel tank has been adopted. The 2017 CBR1000RR SP and CBR1000RR SP2 also featured titanium fuel tanks, but required an outer plastic cover. Advances in titanium pressing and painting technologies have made it possible to eliminate this cover on the new model, contributing to further weight reduction.

Exclusive to the Fireblade SP, the fuel tank features a hand-finished hairline treatment that leaves portions of the titanium surface exposed. This design combines weight reduction with functional beauty, creating a distinctive appearance that enhances the pride of ownership.

A new Honda Flagship WING product emblem, featuring a monotone silver-and-black design, is positioned on both sides of the fuel tank.

Power unit

The 999cm3 liquid-cooled, four-stroke, DOHC, four-valve inline-four engine features a two-stage variable-length intake air funnel system, a first for a mass-produced Honda motorcycle.

The system uses a two-piece intake funnel structure that separates vertically, varying the effective length and diameter of the intake passage according to engine speed. At engine speeds of 11,750rpm and above, the upper funnel slides upward and separates from the lower funnel. This improves power output in the low-to-mid rpm range while maintaining high-rpm performance, contributing to greater ease of use across the entire engine speed range.

The existing two-motor throttle-by-wire system has also been refined. More precise electronic control enables finer adjustment of the throttle valve openings, improving throttle response during acceleration and engine braking performance during deceleration.

These refinements also enable smoother transitions from deceleration to acceleration, enhancing drivability and overall ease of control.

In addition to these improvements, components including the cylinder head cover have been changed from aluminum to magnesium, contributing to a weight reduction of more than 200g on the Fireblade SP.

New HRC Works Edition

The newly introduced HRC Works Edition has been developed to further enhance competitiveness in WSBK. Designed exclusively for solo riding, it incorporates numerous dedicated components.

Its carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP)*3 front winglets, front fender, and rear duct fairing improve aerodynamic performance. Combined with their lightweight construction, these components contribute to improved acceleration and cornering performance.

The suspension features mechanically adjustable Ohlins NPX front forks and TTX36 rear suspension, delivering consistent damping performance and road-holding capability during racetrack riding. Braking is handled by Brembo Hypure Sports components.

The HRC Works Edition also offers the following HRC Racing Kit*4 components to meet racing regulations:

- PGM-FI and ignition unit

- Bottom-neutral shift system

- Head pipe collar

- Swingarm pivot collar

- Other racing components

Adoption of sustainable materials

As part of its efforts to realize a society with zero environmental impact, Honda aims to achieve a 100% sustainable material usage rate by 2050 and is actively expanding the use of recycled and biomass-derived materials.

All variants of the 2027 CBR1000RR-R incorporate four types of sustainable materials.

- Windscreen:

Made from DURABIO(TM),*5 an environmentally responsible, plant-derived engineering plastic. With excellent moldability, weather resistance, and scratch resistance, DURABIO(TM) delivers durability and improved environmental performance without compromising the windscreen's functionality or appearance.

- Front and rear seat bases:

Made using pre-consumer recycled materials derived from manufacturing and molding offcuts generated during the production of automobiles, home appliances, and other products.

- Air cleaner case, side covers, and other components:

Made using post-consumer recycled materials derived from discarded plastic products previously used in households, commercial facilities, and other applications.

- Honda Flagship WING emblem:

Made using chemically recycled acrylic resin produced by breaking down used acrylic materials, including those recovered from end-of-life vehicles, into raw materials for reuse.

*1 FIM: Federation Internationale de Motocyclisme.

*2 For the Fireblade and Fireblade SP variants.

*3 CFRP: Carbon fiber reinforced plastic.

*4 Installing the HRC Racing Kit will void the manufacturer's warranty.

*5 DURABIO(TM) is a registered trademark of Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation.

Source: Honda Motor Co, Ltd

data.title: PROVISIONAL RESULTS OF THE REOPENING OF THE TERMS: OFFEROR REACHED A SHAREHOLDING OF APPROXIMATELY 96.29% OF THE ISSUER'S COMMON SHARE CAPITAL
data.description:
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OR REGULATIONS OF SUCH JURISDICTION

COMMUNICATION PUBLISHED BY IVECO GROUP N.V. UPON REQUEST, IN THE NAME AND ON BEHALF OF TML CV HOLDINGS B.V.

VOLUNTARY TOTALITARIAN TENDER OFFER FOR ALL OF THE COMMON SHARES OF IVECO GROUP N.V.

* * *

PRESS RELEASE

pursuant to Article 36 of the Resolution No. 11971 of 14 May 1999, as further amended and supplemented (the "Issuers' Regulation")

END OF THE REOPENING OF THE TERMS

PROVISIONAL RESULTS OF THE REOPENING OF THE TERMS: OFFEROR REACHED A SHAREHOLDING OF APPROXIMATELY 96.29% OF THE ISSUER'S COMMON SHARE CAPITAL, NET OF TREASURY SHARES

THE PAYMENT DATE UPON COMPLETION OF THE REOPENING OF THE TERMS IS SET FOR 13 NOVEMBER 2026

DUTCH LEGAL SQUEEZE-OUT

* * * * *

Amsterdam, the Netherlands, 6 November 2026 – With reference to the voluntary totalitarian tender offer (the "Offer") promoted by TML CV Holdings Pte. Ltd. ("TML CV HS"), through its wholly-owned company TML CV Holdings B.V. (the "Offeror"), pursuant to Articles 102 et seq. of the Italian Legislative Decree No. 58 of 24 February 1998, as further amended and supplemented (the "CFA"), on all the common shares (the "Common Shares") of Iveco Group N.V. ("IVG" or the "Issuer"), the Offeror hereby announces the following.

Capitalised terms used in this press release, unless otherwise defined, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the offer document relating to the Offer, approved by CONSOB by resolution No. 24119 of 3 September 2026 and published on 4 September 2026 (the "Offer Document"), as well as in the Amendment Notice (as defined below), both available, inter alia, on the Issuer's website (www.ivecogroup.com) and on the Offeror's website (www.tatamotors.com).

It is recalled that the Offer was amended, pursuant to Articles 36 and 43 of the Issuers' Regulation, on 9 October 2026 by means of an increase of the Price through the recognition of an additional cash component equal to EUR 0.30 for each Common Share tendered to the Offer, as announced to the market by means of a press release published on the same date (the "Amendment Notice").

1. Provisional results of the Reopening of the Terms

Based on the provisional results communicated by BNP Paribas, Italian Branch, acting as Intermediary Responsible for Coordinating the Collection of the Acceptances, during the Reopening of the Terms, which ended on the date hereof, No. 18,309,029 Common Shares have been tendered in acceptance of the Offer, representing approximately 6.75% of the Issuer's common share capital and of the Offer Shares (i.e., No. 271,215,400), for an aggregate countervalue (calculated on the basis of the Price, as amended by the Amendment Notice) equal to EUR 263,650,017.60.

In light of the above, should the provisional results of the Reopening of the Terms be confirmed, taking into account (i) the No. 238,157,212 Common Shares already tendered to the Offer during the Acceptance Period (equal to approximately 87.81% of the Issuer's common share capital), (ii) the No. 18,309,029 Common Shares tendered to the Offer during the Reopening of the Terms (equal to approximately 6.75% of the Issuer's common share capital), (iii) the No. 4,868,597 Treasury Shares (equal to approximately 1.80% of the Issuer's common share capital), and (iv) that in the period between the Date of the Offer Document (i.e., 4 September 2026) and the date hereof, the Offeror has not purchased Common Shares outside the Offer, the Offeror will hold No. 256,466,241 Common Shares, equal to approximately 96.29% of the Issuer's common share capital, net of Treasury Shares.

The final results of the Reopening of the Terms will be announced in a separate press release pursuant to Article 41, paragraph 6, of the Issuers' Regulation, which will be issued by the Offeror by 7:29 a.m. (CET) on the Trading Day prior to the Payment Date upon Completion of the Reopening of the Terms (i.e., by 7:29 a.m. (CET) on 12 November 2026) (the "Press Release on the Final Results of the Reopening of the Terms").

2. Price and Payment Date upon Completion of the Reopening of the Terms

The Price for each Common Share tendered in acceptance of the Offer consists of the initial Price indicated in the Offer Document equal to EUR 14.10 (cum dividend), increased by the Additional Price of EUR 0.30 (cum dividend), and therefore is equal to an aggregate amount of EUR 14.40 (cum dividend) per Common Share (the "Price").

The payment of the Price with respect to the Common Shares tendered to the Offer during the Reopening of the Terms – against the simultaneous transfer to the Offeror of the ownership of the Common Shares tendered to the Offer – will take place on 13 November 2026.

3. Dutch Legal Squeeze-Out

Based on the provisional results (if confirmed), in light of the Offeror having reached, together with its Affiliates, an aggregate shareholding at least equal to 95% of the Issuer's issued and outstanding share capital represented by Common Shares (calculated in accordance with the DCC, in any case not taking into account the Treasury Shares), and having declared in the Offer Document its intention not to restore a free float sufficient to ensure the regular trading of the Issuer's Common Shares, the Offeror hereby announces that it will commence the Dutch Legal Squeeze-Out in respect of the remaining Common Shares currently outstanding, and the Dutch Legal Squeeze-Out may be preceded, at the Offeror's election, by the implementation of the Demerger and the Share Sale.

The timing, modalities and terms of the Dutch Legal Squeeze-Out and, if implemented at the Offeror's election, the Demerger and the Share Sale will be communicated to the market in due time by means of a separate press release in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Borsa Italiana will order the suspension of trading in the Common Shares and/or the Delisting pursuant to Article 2.5.1 of the Stock Exchange Regulation, taking into account the time required to complete the Demerger and the Share Sale and/or the Dutch Legal Squeeze-Out.

* * * * *

For further information regarding the Offer, please refer to the Offer Document and the Amendment Notice, both available to the public at:

  • the registered office of the Offeror at Basisweg 10, 1043AP Amsterdam, The Netherlands;
  • the registered office of the Issuer at Via Puglia 35, 10156 Turin, Italy;
  • the registered office of BNP Paribas, Italian Branch, as intermediary responsible for coordinating the collection of the acceptances, at Piazza Lina Bo Bardi 3, 20124 Milan, Italy;
  • the website of Tata Motors at https://cv.tatamotors.com/;
  • the website of the Issuer at https://www.ivecogroup.com/; and
  • the website of Georgeson S.r.l., as global information agent, at www.georgeson.com/it.

* * *

The voluntary totalitarian tender offer referred to in this press release (the "Offer") is promoted by TML CV Holdings Pte. Ltd. ("TML CV HS"), through TML CV Holdings B.V., a company wholly-owned by TML CV HS (the "Offeror") on all issued common shares (the "Common Shares") of Iveco Group N.V. ("IVG" or the "Issuer"). This press release does not constitute either a purchase offer or a solicitation to sell the Common Shares of IVG.

The Offeror has published an offer document (the "Offer Document"), which IVG's shareholders must carefully review. The Offer is addressed, on equal conditions, to all the holders of the Common Shares and is launched in Italy and extended to the United States of America in compliance with Section 14(e) and Regulation 14E of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "U.S. Securities Exchange Act"), subject to the applicable exemptions set forth in Rule 14d-1(d) of the U.S. Securities Exchange Act. Except as indicated below, the Offer is subject to disclosure obligations and procedural requirements provided for by Italian law. US IVG shareholders should be aware that such requirements may differ materially from those applicable under US domestic tender offer law and practice.

In accordance with the laws of, and practice in, Italy and to the extent permitted by applicable law, including Rule 14e-5 under the U.S. Exchange Act, the Offeror, the Offeror's affiliates or any nominees or brokers of the foregoing (acting as agents, or in a similar capacity, for IVG or any of its affiliates, as applicable) may from time to time, and other than pursuant to the Offer, directly or indirectly, purchase, or arrange to purchase, outside of the United States of America, Common Shares in IVG or any securities that are convertible into, exchangeable for or exercisable for such Common Shares in IVG before or during the period in which the Offer remains open for acceptance. These purchases may occur either in the open market at prevailing prices or in private transactions at negotiated prices. To the extent information about such purchases or arrangements to purchase is made public in Italy, such information will be disclosed by means of a press release or other means reasonably calculated to inform US shareholders of IVG of such information. In addition, subject to the applicable laws of Italy and US securities laws, including Rule 14e-5 under the U.S. Exchange Act, the financial advisers to the Offeror or their respective affiliates may also engage in ordinary course trading activities in securities of IVG, which may include purchases or arrangements to purchase such securities.

In order to comply with the rules and exemptions provided by US law, an Offer Document translated into English has been made available to the holders of the Common Shares resident in the United States of America. The English version of the Offer Document is merely a courtesy translation and the Italian version of the Offer Document is the only document submitted to Consob for its approval.

It may not be possible for US shareholders to effect service of process within the United States of America upon IVG, the Offeror or any of their respective affiliates, or their respective officers or directors, some or all of which may reside outside the United States of America, or to enforce against any of them judgments of the United States of America courts predicated upon the civil liability provisions of the federal securities laws of the United States of America or other US law. It may not be possible to bring an action against IVG, the Offeror and/or their respective officers or directors (as applicable) in a non-US court for violations of US laws. Further, it may not be possible to compel the Offeror or IVG or their respective affiliates, as applicable, to subject themselves to the judgment of a US court. In addition, it may be difficult to enforce outside the United States of America original actions, or actions for the enforcement of judgments of US courts, based on the civil liability provisions of the US federal securities laws.

The Offer, if completed, may have consequences under US federal income tax and under applicable U.S. state and local, as well as non-U.S., tax laws. Each shareholder of IVG is urged to consult its independent professional adviser immediately regarding the tax consequences of the Offer.

NEITHER THE U.S. SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION NOR ANY SECURITIES COMMISSION OR OTHER REGULATORY AUTHORITY IN ANY STATE OF THE U.S. HAS APPROVED OR DECLINED TO APPROVE THE OFFER OR THIS ANNOUNCEMENT, PASSED UPON THE FAIRNESS OR MERITS OF THE OFFER OR PROVIDED AN OPINION AS TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY OFFER DOCUMENT. ANY REPRESENTATION TO THE CONTRARY IS A CRIMINAL OFFENCE IN THE UNITED STATES.

The Offer has not been and will not be launched or promoted by the Offeror in Canada, Japan, Australia or in any other country other than Italy and the United States of America in which such Offer is not permitted in absence of the authorisation of the competent authorities or other obligations from the Offeror (such countries, including Canada, Japan and Australia, jointly, the "Other Countries"), nor by using instruments of communication or national or international commerce of the Other Countries (including but not limited to the postal network, fax, telex, email, telephone and internet), nor by way of any structure of any of the financial intermediaries of the Other Countries nor in any other way.

Copy of this press release, or portions of the same, as also copy of any subsequent document which will be issued in connection with the Offer, are not and must not be sent, nor in any way transmitted or distributed, directly or indirectly in the Other Countries. Any party who receives the abovementioned documents must not distribute, send or transmit them (either by post nor by any other method or instrument of communication or commerce) in the Other Countries.

This press release, as well as any other document that has or will be issued in connection with the Offer does not constitute and cannot be interpreted as an offer to purchase or solicitation of an offer to sell financial instruments to parties resident in Other Countries. No instrument may be offered or sold in the Other Countries in the absence of specific authorisation in compliance with the applicable provisions of the local law of those countries or in derogation of those provisions. Tenders in the Offer by parties resident in countries other than Italy and the United States of America may be subject to specific obligations or restrictions provided by law or regulatory provisions. Parties who wish to take part in the Offer bear the exclusive responsibility to comply with those laws and therefore prior to tendering their Common Shares in the Offer, those parties are required to verify their possible existence and applicability, consulting their own advisors.
